Zero-float exact-Q rational congruence pipeline combining shear-pivoted multiaffine Hessian inertia certificates, dual up-down Dirichlet-Gram spectral-gap certificates, and rational Taylor-envelope matrix concentration certificates across non-representable V_8 (Theorems 3.2-3.3).
summary: This manuscript operationalizes recent Lorentzian polynomial and matrix entropy contraction theory (Brändén-Huh 2020; Ercan, Nov 2026 [4]) into exact-Q algebraic certificates and a zero-float verification pipeline (LORENTZ-MATROID-CERT-1.0) backed by 18 zero-dependency Lean 4 algebraic lemmas. Theorem 3.1 establishes an exact coincident phase transition on G_{eps,m} = (K_m \sqcup K_m) + eps K_{m,m} where Lorentzianity holds iff gamma(P_{2->1->2}) >= 1/2 iff eps >= (m-1)/m. Theorem 3.2 develops O(k^3) exact-Q congruence diagonalization with shear pivots to certify zero-diagonal matroid link Hessians and dual up-down Dirichlet-Gram spectral gaps across U_{3,6}, M(K_4), F_7, F_7^-, and non-representable V_8. Theorem 3.3 certifies finite-instance subgaussian matrix concentration tails purely over Q (conditional on Ercan [4]). All mathematical proofs and numerical quantities visible in the PDF are sound and consistent; limitations pertain to the modest theoretical depth beyond [2,4] and the fact that Lean 4 covers only the scalar/diagonal algebraic core rather than the full matrix-spectral or Python verification layers.
weaknesses: Analytical novelty is incremental relative to Brändén-Huh [2] and Ercan [4]: Theorem 3.1 is a clean block-matrix calculation on one explicit 2-homogeneous family (not a general converse), and Theorems 3.2-3.3 apply classical symmetric congruence and Taylor series truncation to wrap Ercan's theorem.

The Lean 4 formalization covers 18 scalar, integer-list, and rational algebraic lemmas (Table 1) rather than the 2m x 2m matrix spectrum of Theorem 3.1, the O(n^3) congruence algorithm or Cauchy interlacing in Theorem 3.2, operator norms over R^d in Theorem 3.3, or the Python verifier itself.
Definition 2.2 includes l=0 (where |I_0|=1 and Q_{0->r->0} is 1x1 so lambda_2 is undefined), and Theorem 3.2(2) implicitly requires k >= 2.
Theorem 3.3 restricts observables {A_e} to real symmetric rational matrices in Q^{d x d} rather than general complex Hermitian matrices (which would require 2d x 2d real embedding).
Exact rational congruence runs in O(k^3) field operations without bit-length bounds in Theorem 3.2, limiting scalability to moderate-sized matroids as acknowledged in Section 6.
